newsitem.title: GERMANY: Two Germans sentenced for kidnap of millionaire.
newsitem.headline: Two Germans sentenced for kidnap of millionaire.

text.p: A German court on Friday sentenced two men to long jail terms for the kidnapping of a Hamburg multi-millionaire whose family paid the largest ransom in German criminal history to secure his release.

The court sentenced Wolfgang Koszics, 55, to 10 and a half years in jail and his 59-year-old accomplice, Peter Richter, to five years for last year's kidnapping of Jan Philipp Reemstma, the former owner of Germany's second largest tobacco firm.
Both men had confessed to their parts in the crime.
The sentences were less than the 12 years prosecutors had demanded for Koszics and the five and a half years for Richter.
The judge said Koszics had planned the kidnapping along with the head of the gang, Thomas Drach, who is still at large.
Koszics kept watch on Reemtsma while he was locked in a cellar for five weeks and also organised the handover of the 30 million mark ($17.8 million) ransom.
Richter kept contact with Reemtsma's family during the abduction and named the conditions for the handover of the ransom, the judge said.

The 43-year-old was blindfolded and taken to a cottage near Bremen, where he was kept chained up in a cellar. Police imposed a news blackout at the time and communicated with the kidnappers through the personal columns of a Hamburg newspaper.
Richter and Koszics were arrested in Spain. Police are still hunting for Drach, and most of the ransom.
Reemstma sold his majority share of the family empire in 1980 and has since devoted much of his time and money to academic research and sponsorship of the arts.
